glossary.definition: Reinforcement learning is a training method where an AI learns by trial and error: it takes an action, and gets rewarded or penalized depending on the outcome. It's essentially how you'd train a dog with treats, the dog doesn't understand English instructions, but it learns "sit" earns a treat and jumping on the guest doesn't, purely from repeated feedback. It's used both in robotics, like a robot learning to walk, and in shaping how chatbots respond to people.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly in early talks to buy, acquihire or invest more in Reflection AI
items.summary: Nvidia Corp. is in early talks to acquire open-weight model developer Reflection AI Inc. or invest more in the startup, according to the Financial Times. People familiar with the matter told the paper that an agreement could come within weeks. The talks could still collapse.

items.title: Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success?
items.summary: Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product, but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date. Apple will announce a new smart home hub on Tuesday called the HomeView, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman . Gurman described the HomeView as a Siri-powered device with a display and an A18 chip, allowing customers to control their other smart home devices. The HomeView will reportedly be available in two models — one designed for countertops and the other to be mounted on walls.

items.title: Why AI agents might not be right for you
items.summary: There’s no question that 2026 is the year of the artificial intelligence agent. AI agents are remarkably ubiquitous, as people use them to write code, communicate with customers, identify and resolve issues in their information technology environments, and execute complex tasks within enterprise environments. It seems there’s nothing that agents cannot do. And yet, the risks inherent in agentic behavior are in the news almost as much as their success stories.

items.title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI
items.summary: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as " super intelligence ," you'd be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on. While most of the broader population is sticking with AI, some of Silicon Valley's most powerful are falling in line and trying to give Trump the great AI rebrand he so desires. That Elon Musk was quick to jump on board , promising to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, isn't surprising. Musk, Benioff, Huang, and now Nadella have all capitulated to Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand.

items.title: AI agent teams waste massive tokens for barely measurable quality gains, research finds
items.summary: Teams of AI agents barely outperform solo agents but cost up to 5.1x more, according to Vals AI. Only one out of four tests with GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 showed a measurable gain. Anthropic's own data backs this up: beyond ten agents, quality plateaus while token costs keep climbing. AI agent teams deliver almost no better results than single agents, research finds.

items.title: AI agents overstate their results and remain far from autonomous research, study finds
items.summary: Epoch AI and Anthropic independently found the same thing: current AI models like GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5 can run experiments but lack scientific self-criticism and genuine creative thinking. At best, Sol reached 15 percent of the human reference score, and even that came from methods researchers already knew. The models' biggest weakness is still their inability to critically question their own results. Results from Epoch AI and Anthropic show that AI models can run experiments but lack scientific self-criticism and genuine creative thinking.

items.title: I Made Terrible Games With Google’s AI Playground
items.summary: A long day’s haul in the video game slop mines. Neon Don is really pissed at his ex-wife’s lawyer. He’ll tell you any chance he gets while he shotguns lines of pixelated bad guys. He’s also not real—his likeness has only existed for a few minutes in a top-down cyberpunk-style shooter game, generated in the Google Labs service Playground .

items.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
items.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of. Is this tech so useful that it's worth throwing gobs of money at a computer or a laptop with lots of overpriced RAM? I'll try to help you find out.

items.title: AI Is Getting Really Good at Messing With Cybercriminals
items.summary: Anti-cybercrime initiatives are increasingly using AI to scam the scammers by tricking them into talking to lifelike bots that they think are real victims. Even as AI supercharges digital scamming and cybercrime, it’s also being recruited in the fight to protect potential victims. Governments around the world have consistently struggled to address the global crisis of online crime, grappling with the limitations of attempting to crack down on criminals beyond their borders . This has inspired alternative efforts, like using automation to attempt to go after scammers en masse—perhaps by spamming the spammers to squander their resources.
